body: Case 2: The premise is wrong, Cashu-TS 4.13.1 is correct to remove a partial (incomplete) DLEQ and treat the proof as not having one. A proof with no DLEQ can still be valid, spendable ecash, it just cannot be determined as so without attempting a swap.

Thanks for the report. As noted above, case 2 is not an issue and case 1 does not go through the app's receive flow, which already runs a residue check when a mint is added or activated. There are two gaps in that check though, so keeping this open to track them.

The plan is to wait for cashu-ts 4.14, which backports `findLegacyDerivationCollisions` (cashubtc/cashu-ts#1488), then:

1. Replace the hand-rolled check with the helper. It only compares legacy (`00` and base64) ids, so V2 keysets drop out of the comparison, and it covers same-mint rotations. Collisions get a specific error instead of the generic "Mint validation error".
2. Rethrow that error from the hourly keyset refresh before a swap, instead of continuing on stale keysets as it does for connection errors.
3. Re-run the check before retrying after cashu-ts repairs its keyset snapshot, since that path refreshes keysets without going through the add/activate check.

Agree a collision should block, not warn, as it is not something a user will know what to do with.

Have the coding agent verify with a regression test that pauses the update after its read, commits removal, then resumes the update and asserts both rows remain absent. `src/components/HistoryTable.vue:479`, `src/stores/transactionWorker.ts:798`, `src/stores/paymentHistory.ts:424`, `src/stores/paymentHistory.ts:439`, `src/stores/paymentHistory.ts:445`, `src/stores/paymentHistory.ts:592`
